exercise1.prompt: One type and one block of memory buys arithmetic on the whole column.

hiddenCases.name: no loop is needed
hiddenCases.describe: the arithmetic applied to the whole array at once

exercise1.hint: np.array(scores) + 5. The addition reaches every element on its own, which is the point of the array.

questions.prompt: What does [1, 2, 3] * 2 give you in plain Python?
questions.explain: Multiplying a list repeats it. Only an array reads * 2 as "double every element", which is the first thing that surprises people coming from lists.

questions.prompt: Why can numpy add a large array faster than a Python loop can?
choices: One type in one block of memory means the addition runs in compiled code, not per object
questions.explain: A list element is an object with its own type to check. An array is a known type laid out end to end, so the work happens once in C rather than a million times in Python.

questions.prompt: What does an array give up compared with a list?
choices: Holding several different types at once
questions.explain: The single dtype is the trade. An array of mixed types has to widen to something that fits everything, usually object, and the speed goes with it.
